docs.text: Kubernetes libraries ¶ The Kubernetes packages provide typed Unobin resources grouped by Kubernetes API group and version, plus a dynamic library for built-in and custom objects. Import the packages a factory uses and share one Kubernetes configuration between their aliases when they connect to the same cluster. factory: { imports: { core: 'github.com/cloudboss/unobin-library-kubernetes//api/core/v1' } library-configs: { core: {} } resources: { settings: core.config-map { object: { metadata: { name: 'settings' } data: { greeting: 'hello' } } } } outputs: { name: { value: resource.settings.object.metadata.name } } } Configuration ¶ All packages use library-config('github.com/cloudboss/unobin-library-kubernetes//config') . Configuration follows client-go loading rules: KUBECONFIG selects kubeconfig files to merge, and ~/.kube/config is the default when it is unset. An empty configuration also supports in-cluster ServiceAccount credentials. The library supports kubeconfig contexts, certificates and keys, bearer tokens, OIDC, and exec credential plugins. Paths and inline certificate data retain kubeconfig's conventions. Exec helpers must be available to the compiled factory. Pass a configuration input to several aliases to use the same cluster: inputs: { kubernetes-config: { type: library-config('github.com/cloudboss/unobin-library-kubernetes//config') default: {} } } imports: { core: 'github.com/cloudboss/unobin-library-kubernetes//api/core/v1' apps: 'github.com/cloudboss/unobin-library-kubernetes//api/apps/v1' } library-configs: { core: input.kubernetes-config apps: input.kubernetes-config } See the configuration reference for all fields and sensitivity declarations. Typed resources ¶ Typed libraries expose explicit schemas and resource-specific mutation and wait behavior. Namespaced typed resources default to the default namespace unless their metadata selects another namespace. Cluster-scoped resources use their cluster endpoint. The generated reference lists each registered resource, its inputs and outputs, defaults, constraints, and sensitive fields. Its descriptions come from Go documentation comments next to the implementation. Core v1 Apps v1 All libraries Dynamic objects ¶ The dynamic library accepts a structured manifest for a built-in or custom Kubernetes object. It uses server-side apply with field ownership, conflict controls, and UID protection. CRDs must be established and discoverable before their custom objects are applied. Use the object reference for its schema and lifecycle controls. See architecture for implementation ownership and API group boundaries.

docs.text: Kubernetes library architecture ¶ This repository contains a collection of importable Unobin libraries in one Go module. Public package paths follow Kubernetes API groups and versions. The module has one release version; a Kubernetes API version such as apps/v1 is a separate part of the public contract. Public libraries ¶ Package Purpose Example exports config Shared cluster and authentication configuration Configuration schema dynamic Generic manifest-based object management object api/core/v1 Core API objects config-map , namespace , secret , service , pod api/apps/v1 Workload controllers deployment , stateful-set , daemon-set api/batch/v1 Batch workloads job , cron-job api/networking/v1 Networking policy and ingress network-policy , ingress api/rbac/v1 Roles and bindings role , role-binding , cluster-role api/storage/v1 Storage configuration storage-class , csi-driver api/autoscaling/v2 Autoscaling horizontal-pod-autoscaler api/policy/v1 Disruption policy pod-disruption-budget api/coordination/v1 Lease objects lease api/apiextensions/v1 Custom resource definitions custom-resource-definition The example exports define the destination for future constructs. A typed library starts with its configuration and compatibility declarations and gains exports only when their implementations and tests are complete. An empty library does not claim support for the example kinds. Each public package defines Library() in library.go . Registration names are local to that package. Importing //api/apps/v1 as apps makes a Deployment available as apps.deployment once that construct is implemented. Resource, data source, and action registrations remain separate categories. Singular data sources use the same export name as the corresponding resource. For example, core.config-map creates a ConfigMap in resources and reads one in data-sources . Plural names such as core.nodes identify collection lookups. Short group directory names follow the Kubernetes Go API packages. The actual group strings remain exact: networking.k8s.io , rbac.authorization.k8s.io , and apiextensions.k8s.io , for example. The core directory represents the empty group, whose API version is v1 . The apiextensions types come from k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/apis/apiextensions/v1 . CRD definitions belong to api/apiextensions/v1 . Custom resource instances use the group and served version declared by their CRD. The dynamic library supports those instances without a typed binding for each operator. Configuration and naming ¶ Every public library uses config.LibraryConfiguration() and the same config.Configuration Go type. A factory can declare one library-config('github.com/cloudboss/unobin-library-kubernetes//config') input and bind it to several imported aliases in library-configs . Different aliases can use different cluster configurations. All Unobin fields use strict kebab case. Let the SDK derive names from Go fields; use struct tags for sensitivity. Conversion to Kubernetes objects handles native JSON names. Kubeconfig files retain their Kubernetes formats. Structured manifests retain native Kubernetes field names. Client-go loading rules, authentication, and standard environment variables remain the configuration contract. Implementation ownership ¶ config/ Public configuration entry point dynamic/ Public generic-object entry point api/<group>/<version>/ Public typed registrations and schema tests internal/client/ Configuration loading, discovery, and dynamic clients internal/object/ Object identity, field selection, and deletion helpers internal/api/<group>/<version>/ Typed resource, data source, and action implementations tests/compile/ Shared configuration compile fixture tests/integration/scenarios/ API and compiled-factory scenarios Typed implementations use category suffixes such as ConfigMapResource , ConfigMapResourceOutput , and DeploymentDataSource . Public packages contain registration code and schema tests. Construct behavior and focused tests belong in the matching internal package. Common helpers provide client selection, saved-target identity, UID checks, managed-field projection, and deletion waits. They allow each construct to choose the mutation operation established by its contract. A typed resource can require create, update, JSON Patch, merge patch, or server-side apply. The generic manifest resource's apply policy is one implementation choice. object.Connect selects the dynamic resource interface, server, and namespace. object.TargetClient selects a saved target with current credentials. object.CheckUID checks the immutable object identity. object.Delete enforces the saved UID and waits for deletion while preserving the caller's propagation, grace-period, and resource-version options. object.OwnedFields and object.FieldValues provide stable projection for server-side apply users. Inputs and outputs have explicit Unobin schemas. Typed bindings convert those values to the pinned Kubernetes API representation. Read-only server metadata must not become writable inputs merely because it appears in an upstream Go struct. Stable identity and managed values belong in resource outputs. Status, resource versions, timestamps, and raw managed-fields metadata must not cause updates just because a controller changed them. Data sources can expose live status. Deployment waits for rollout by default during create and update. An additional wait action does not replace a resource's required wait. Waits can observe status without persisting volatile status in resource drift outputs. Checks and fixtures ¶ Put Unobin fixtures in package-local testdata/ub/ files. Schema and registration checks exercise the public SDK contract. Behavior tests cover lifecycle choices; they do not inspect documentation or tooling text. Integration scenarios group constructs by API group and version under tests/integration/scenarios/ . Each scenario can include a factory, initial and updated configurations, and a Kubernetes verifier. The shared driver compiles the factory with the local library, pins both configurations, plans and applies them, and destroys the stack. The verifier can save object identities in VERIFY_BUILD_DIR to check whether an update preserved or replaced an object. Integration checks run through each scenario's verify/ executable. API checks and compiled fixture checks return errors and clean up temporary objects. Verifier fixtures belong in package-local testdata/ub/ files. Final construct validation includes build, unit tests, vet, lint, and the focused kind scenario: make build make test make vet make lint SCENARIO = core-v1 make test-integration-kind Use SCENARIO=apps-v1 to check Deployment, StatefulSet, and DaemonSet in kind. A local API server can verify API behavior. Rollout waits require workload controllers and running Pods. Run existing-cluster scenarios only with explicit authorization. docs.text: custom-resource-definition resource ¶ Description ¶ CustomResourceDefinitionResource manages a cluster-scoped custom API definition. It owns the complete desired specification, labels and annotations. Dependent instances can use dynamic.object after establishment and discovery complete. docs.text: StatefulSetResource manages one apps/v1 StatefulSet. It saves server, namespace, name and UID, and uses current credentials for that saved identity. Create and update wait for rollout by default. API or wait errors fail the operation; a completed write can remain remote after failure. This resource does not manage Services, Pods or PVCs. selector, service-name and template with metadata. Template spec is optional; Kubernetes checks containers, selector compatibility and workload settings. Policy, revision history, selector, service name, claim templates and inherited pod identity fields require replacement for effective changes. Omitted computed members retain remote values; removing optional-only immutable fields requires replacement. Replicas is nullable signed decimal text with no default. Create requires int32 text; updates send the parsed integer to Kubernetes. Revision history compares original integers before the create int32 cast. Omitted revision history sends zero on create; explicit values must be positive. Min-ready-seconds defaults to zero and is ignored during create without claim templates. Claim templates are an ordered immutable list with full metadata, default namespace default, access-mode sets and quantity resources. Empty storage-class-name is omitted. An omitted strategy uses API defaults and is excluded from outputs. A present strategy defaults to RollingUpdate; a present rolling-update defaults partition to zero. OnDelete and negative partitions reach API validation. Partition casts to int32 on create; updates and equality use the original integer. Removing the configured strategy fails. A present retention policy defaults both actions to Retain; omission retains observation. Pod defaults include restart Always, DNS ClusterFirst, automount and service links true, grace 30 seconds, and host/process flags false. OnFailure and Never are accepted for API validation. Containers default termination path /dev/termination-log, boolean flags false and mount propagation None, port protocol TCP, probe thresholds 3/1, period 10 and timeout 1. Image pull policy, resources, termination policy and container restart policy retain observation on omission. Present security blocks default allow-privilege-escalation true, privileged and read-only root false, seccomp Unconfined and Windows host-process false. Volume modes default 0644; projected token expiration defaults 3600. Local and ceph-fs volume settings and local secret namespaces are accepted but ineffective. Azure File secret namespace still requires replacement. Quantities compare numerically; sets ignore order and duplicates, while lists retain order. Explicit zero, false and empty computed collections are kept. wait-for-rollout optional(boolean) WaitForRollout defaults to true for create and every update, including metadata changes. Rollout first requires ready replicas to equal desired replicas, then RollingUpdate and a nonzero observed generation at least equal to generation. Rolling partitions use updated replicas; without a rolling object completion uses revision equality. False skips polling and still performs the final GET. API errors stop polling immediately. create-timeout optional(string) CreateTimeout is a positive Go duration, default 10m, shared by POST, wait and final GET. read-timeout optional(string) ReadTimeout is a positive Go duration, default 10m, for standalone reads. update-timeout optional(string) UpdateTimeout bounds the live read, PATCH, rollout wait and final GET; default 10m. delete-timeout optional(string) DeleteTimeout is a positive Go duration, default 10m, read from prior input on deletion. ignore-annotations optional(list(string)) IgnoreAnnotations filters only untracked outer read keys by regular expression. ignore-labels optional(list(string)) IgnoreLabels filters only untracked outer read keys by regular expression.

docs.text: Configuration ¶ This library uses library-config('github.com/cloudboss/unobin-library-kubernetes//config') for per-alias settings. Pass a value to library-configs: in factory source, usually from a factory input so stack files can choose the environment-specific settings. docs.text: run-cron-job action ¶ Description ¶ RunCronJobAction runs an existing CronJob template under an explicit invocation name. An unchanged action skips. Change job-name to request another Job, or @trigger to observe the same Job again. Removal never deletes the Job. CronJob ownership, history limits and inherited TTL can later remove it; disappearance cannot prove completion. Manual creation bypasses the source schedule, suspension and concurrency policy. Reusing a name requires the same source UID and template fingerprint. A deleted Job can later be created under the same name; this is not durable execution history. Failure, deletion or replacement while waiting returns an error. Failed Jobs remain available for inspection. The complete Job template is copied with CronJob ownership. Source: internal/api/batch/v1/run_cron_job_action.go:33 Example usage: imports: { kubernetes-batch-v1: 'github.com/cloudboss/unobin-library-kubernetes//api/batch/v1' } actions: { example: kubernetes-batch-v1.run-cron-job { # Set input fields here. } } Inputs ¶ cron-job-name string required job-name string required namespace optional(string) Namespace defaults to the configured kubeconfig or library namespace. expected-cron-job-uid optional(string) ExpectedCronJobUID optionally guards the source identity. wait-for-completion optional(boolean) default true WaitForCompletion defaults true. False returns a verified Job without checking completion. timeout optional(string) default 10m Timeout bounds Kubernetes HTTP requests and polling; defaults to 10m for source lookup, creation and completion together. Input Constraints ¶ Cron job name rules Requirement. Rule logic Require @core.is-match(input.cron-job-name, '^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?(\\.[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?)*$') && @core.length(input.cron-job-name) <= 253 Job name rules Requirement. Rule logic Require @core.is-match(input.job-name, '^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?(\\.[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?)*$') && @core.length(input.job-name) <= 63 Namespace rules Requirement. Rule logic Require @core.is-match(input.namespace, '^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?$') && @core.length(input.namespace ?? '') <= 63 Expected cron job uid rules Conditional requirement. Rule logic When input.expected-cron-job-uid != null Require @core.length(input.expected-cron-job-uid) >= 1 Timeout rules If set, timeout must be a positive duration. Rule logic Require @core.is-format(input.timeout, 'positive-duration') Outputs ¶ server string namespace string cron-job-name string cron-job-uid string job-name string job-uid string completed boolean

docs.text: job resource ¶ Description ¶ JobResource manages a namespaced Job with completion waits enabled by default. Failed completion returns an error without deleting the created Job. A completion wait that observes a missing Job returns its last successful API values. Standalone reads have a 20m budget and never wait for completion. docs.text: JobResource manages a namespaced Job with completion waits enabled by default. Failed completion returns an error without deleting the created Job. A completion wait that observes a missing Job returns its last successful API values. Standalone reads have a 20m budget and never wait for completion. docs.text: lease resource ¶ Description ¶ LeaseResource manages a namespaced Lease object. It does not elect a leader, renew a lease, or determine expiration. Each configured spec field and metadata key is managed independently; other live values are preserved. Explicit renewal times are managed values and can cause updates. create-timeout optional(string) default 5m CreateTimeout bounds requests and refresh; defaults to 5m. update-timeout optional(string) default 5m UpdateTimeout bounds requests, retries and refresh; defaults to 5m. delete-timeout optional(string) default 5m DeleteTimeout bounds deletion and disappearance waiting; defaults to 5m. docs.text: service resource ¶ Description ¶ ServiceResource manages a namespaced Kubernetes Service. It creates with POST, updates individual fields with JSON Patch, and deletes with a UID precondition. Reads, updates, and deletion use the saved server and identity with current credentials. Kubernetes validates cross-field restrictions and port names. Live load-balancer endpoints remain available in status. Endpoint changes can cause reconciliation, which refreshes outputs without a mutation. Source: internal/api/core/v1/service_types.go:9 Example usage: imports: { kubernetes-core-v1: 'github.com/cloudboss/unobin-library-kubernetes//api/core/v1' } resources: { example: kubernetes-core-v1.service { # Set input fields here. } } Inputs ¶ metadata object object({ name: optional(string) generate-name: optional(string) namespace: optional(string) annotations: optional(map(string)) labels: optional(map(string)) }) required Metadata is required. Exactly one nonempty name or generate-name is required. Namespace defaults to default. Changes to name, generate-name, or effective namespace replace the Service. Generated names come from the API response. Annotation and label maps contain strings. Tracked keys use actual API values even when an internal-key or ignore filter matches. Updates from a nonempty projected map change individual keys and preserve hidden keys. The first insertion into an empty projected map replaces the whole map, including hidden keys. spec object object({ type: optional(string) allocate-load-balancer-node-ports: optional(boolean) cluster-ip: optional(string) cluster-ips: optional(list(string)) external-ips: optional(list(string)) external-name: optional(string) external-traffic-policy: optional(string) internal-traffic-policy: optional(string) ip-families: optional(list(string)) ip-family-policy: optional(string) load-balancer-class: optional(string) load-balancer-ip: optional(string) load-balancer-source-ranges: optional(list(string)) health-check-node-port: optional(integer) publish-not-ready-addresses: optional(boolean) selector: optional(map(string)) session-affinity: optional(string) session-affinity-config: optional( object({ client-ip: optional( object({ timeout-seconds: optional(integer) }) ) }) ) port: optional( list( object({ port: integer name: optional(string) app-protocol: optional(string) protocol: optional(string) node-port: optional(integer) target-port: optional(string) }) ) ) }) required Spec is required. Type defaults to ClusterIP, protocol to TCP, affinity to None, allocation to true, and publish-not-ready-addresses to false. Cluster addresses, traffic policies, IP families and policy, target ports, node ports, and affinity timeout are computed after omission. Ordered port, cluster-ips, and ip-families lists retain order. External-ips and load-balancer-source-ranges are sets. Omitted or empty port lists create no ports and clear old ports on update; each entry requires port 1–65535. Target-port is a string: int32 text becomes a number in Kubernetes JSON. Protocol is case-sensitive TCP, UDP, or SCTP. Node-port accepts 0–65535; configured health-check-node-port accepts 1–65535. Cluster-ip and each cluster-ips member accept an IP or None. Cluster-ips and ip-families have at most two ordered entries. Families are IPv4 or IPv6. Family policy is SingleStack, PreferDualStack, or RequireDualStack. Traffic policies are Cluster or Local. External IPs and source CIDRs are validated locally. Explicit node-port zero requests allocation. Omitted computed port values survive list updates. Empty app-protocol is omitted. Configured cluster-ip, cluster-ips, load-balancer-class, and health-check-node-port changes replace the Service. Omitted computed values retain allocations. Allocation and class are sent on creation only for LoadBalancer. IP-family changes remain subject to API validation. Affinity configuration preserves absent and explicit nested objects; an explicit empty client-ip requests timeout zero, while configured timeout-seconds must be 1–86400. Kubernetes applies its remote default. wait-for-load-balancer optional(boolean) WaitForLoadBalancer defaults to true. Only creation of a returned LoadBalancer waits, until its ingress list has at least one entry. Update never waits. Wait API errors are terminal. Failure returns an error and the latest three unique Service Warning messages, without rollback. create-timeout optional(string) CreateTimeout is a positive Go duration and defaults to 10m. Read, update, and deletion use 20m. Earlier caller cancellation bounds every operation. Deletion waits until the managed UID disappears and preserves finalizers. ignore-annotations optional(list(string)) IgnoreAnnotations contains regexes matched against untracked annotation keys. Tracked keys retain their actual remote values. Internal Kubernetes keys are hidden except the app.kubernetes.io and service.beta.kubernetes.io hosts; ignore regexes still apply to them. ignore-labels optional(list(string)) IgnoreLabels applies the same rules as ignore-annotations to label keys. docs.text: ServiceResource manages a namespaced Kubernetes Service. It creates with POST, updates individual fields with JSON Patch, and deletes with a UID precondition. Reads, updates, and deletion use the saved server and identity with current credentials. Kubernetes validates cross-field restrictions and port names. Live load-balancer endpoints remain available in status. Endpoint changes can cause reconciliation, which refreshes outputs without a mutation. Source: internal/api/core/v1/service_types.go:9 Example usage: imports: { kubernetes-core-v1: 'github.com/cloudboss/unobin-library-kubernetes//api/core/v1' } resources: { example: kubernetes-core-v1.service { # Set input fields here. } }

docs.text: metadata object object({ name: optional(string) generate-name: optional(string) namespace: optional(string) annotations: optional(map(string)) labels: optional(map(string)) }) required Metadata is required. Exactly one nonempty name or generate-name is required. Namespace defaults to default. Changes to name, generate-name, or effective namespace replace the Service. Generated names come from the API response. Annotation and label maps contain strings. Tracked keys use actual API values even when an internal-key or ignore filter matches. Updates from a nonempty projected map change individual keys and preserve hidden keys. The first insertion into an empty projected map replaces the whole map, including hidden keys. spec object object({ type: optional(string) allocate-load-balancer-node-ports: optional(boolean) cluster-ip: optional(string) cluster-ips: optional(list(string)) external-ips: optional(list(string)) external-name: optional(string) external-traffic-policy: optional(string) internal-traffic-policy: optional(string) ip-families: optional(list(string)) ip-family-policy: optional(string) load-balancer-class: optional(string) load-balancer-ip: optional(string) load-balancer-source-ranges: optional(list(string)) health-check-node-port: optional(integer) publish-not-ready-addresses: optional(boolean) selector: optional(map(string)) session-affinity: optional(string) session-affinity-config: optional( object({ client-ip: optional( object({ timeout-seconds: optional(integer) }) ) }) ) port: optional( list( object({ port: integer name: optional(string) app-protocol: optional(string) protocol: optional(string) node-port: optional(integer) target-port: optional(string) }) ) ) }) required Spec is required. Type defaults to ClusterIP, protocol to TCP, affinity to None, allocation to true, and publish-not-ready-addresses to false. Cluster addresses, traffic policies, IP families and policy, target ports, node ports, and affinity timeout are computed after omission. Ordered port, cluster-ips, and ip-families lists retain order. External-ips and load-balancer-source-ranges are sets. Omitted or empty port lists create no ports and clear old ports on update; each entry requires port 1–65535. Target-port is a string: int32 text becomes a number in Kubernetes JSON. Protocol is case-sensitive TCP, UDP, or SCTP. Node-port accepts 0–65535; configured health-check-node-port accepts 1–65535. Cluster-ip and each cluster-ips member accept an IP or None. Cluster-ips and ip-families have at most two ordered entries. Families are IPv4 or IPv6. Family policy is SingleStack, PreferDualStack, or RequireDualStack. Traffic policies are Cluster or Local. External IPs and source CIDRs are validated locally. Explicit node-port zero requests allocation. Omitted computed port values survive list updates. Empty app-protocol is omitted. Configured cluster-ip, cluster-ips, load-balancer-class, and health-check-node-port changes replace the Service. Omitted computed values retain allocations. Allocation and class are sent on creation only for LoadBalancer. IP-family changes remain subject to API validation. Affinity configuration preserves absent and explicit nested objects; an explicit empty client-ip requests timeout zero, while configured timeout-seconds must be 1–86400. Kubernetes applies its remote default. wait-for-load-balancer optional(boolean) WaitForLoadBalancer defaults to true. Only creation of a returned LoadBalancer waits, until its ingress list has at least one entry. Update never waits. Wait API errors are terminal. Failure returns an error and the latest three unique Service Warning messages, without rollback. create-timeout optional(string) CreateTimeout is a positive Go duration and defaults to 10m. Read, update, and deletion use 20m. Earlier caller cancellation bounds every operation. Deletion waits until the managed UID disappears and preserves finalizers. ignore-annotations optional(list(string)) IgnoreAnnotations contains regexes matched against untracked annotation keys. Tracked keys retain their actual remote values. Internal Kubernetes keys are hidden except the app.kubernetes.io and service.beta.kubernetes.io hosts; ignore regexes still apply to them. ignore-labels optional(list(string)) IgnoreLabels applies the same rules as ignore-annotations to label keys.

docs.text: api-resources data source ¶ Description ¶ APIResourcesDataSource queries fresh API discovery with the configured identity.
